types.name: AccessToken
types.description: An access token that grants to the holder the privileges of the user who created it.

fields.description:

fields.description: If non-null, the token may no longer be used after this date.

fields.description:
The last 5 characters of the token, useful for identifying which token is configured.
Only available for tokens created starting with Sourcegraph 6.13.

types.name: AuthProvider
types.description:
A provider of user authentication, such as an external single-sign-on service (e.g., using OpenID Connect or
SAML). The provider information in this type is visible to all viewers and does not contain any secret values.

fields.name: serviceType
fields.description: The type of the auth provider.

fields.name: configID
fields.description:
A stable identifier for this provider's configuration, derived deterministically
from the provider's config without requiring network I/O. Used together with
serviceType to uniquely identify a provider for mutations.

fields.name: serviceID
fields.description: An identifier for the service that the auth provider represents.

fields.name: clientID
fields.description: An identifier for the client of the service that the auth provider represents.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: The human-readable name of the provider.

fields.name: isBuiltin
fields.description: Whether this auth provider is the builtin username-password auth provider.

fields.name: authenticationURL
fields.description: A URL that, when visited, initiates the authentication process for this auth provider.

fields.name: isSignInEnabled
fields.description: Whether this auth provider is currently enabled for sign-in (not hidden and not marked as noSignIn).

fields.name: isPermissionsProvider
fields.description:
Whether this auth provider can be used for repository permissions syncing.
This is true for code host auth providers (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Bitbucket Server, Gerrit, Azure DevOps).

fields.name: enforceAccountConnection
fields.description:
Whether users must connect an external account for this provider before they
can continue using Sourcegraph. Only applies to permissions providers whose
code host enforces repository permissions.

fields.name: hidden
fields.description: Whether this auth provider is hidden from the sign-in page.

fields.name: supportsSignIn
fields.description:
Whether this auth provider supports sign-in. Some providers (e.g. Gerrit) are
permissions-only and cannot be used for sign-in even if configured.

fields.name: order
fields.description:
The display order of this provider on the sign-in page. Providers with lower
order values appear first. Null means no explicit order is set.

types.description:
A change request, such as a GitHub pull request, synchronized from a code host.
It may belong to a repository that is not in Sourcegraph's repository catalog.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique ID of the change request.

fields.name: codeHost
fields.description: The kind of code host on which the change request exists.

fields.name: codeHostURL
fields.description: The base URL of the code host on which the change request exists.

fields.name: externalRepositoryID
fields.description: The code host's identifier for the change request's repository.

fields.name: repositoryName
fields.description:
The name of the change request's repository on the code host, such as
owner/name.

fields.name: repositoryArchived
fields.description:
Whether the change request's repository is archived, or otherwise
read-only, on the code host. Always false on code hosts without archived
repositories.

fields.name: repository
fields.description:
The Sourcegraph repository mirroring the change request's repository, or
null if it is not synchronized to Sourcegraph or the viewer cannot access it.
Use repository.comparison(base: baseOID, head: headOID) to load its diff.
Currently supports GitHub.

fields.name: externalID
fields.description:
The change request's number within its repository, such as a pull request
number.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The change request's URL on the code host.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The change request's title.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
The change request's description as raw, unsanitized code-host markup.
Clients must sanitize it before rendering it as HTML.

fields.name: state
fields.description: The change request's state.

fields.name: draft
fields.description: Whether the change request is a draft.

fields.name: author
fields.description: The code-host user who opened the change request.

fields.name: assignees
fields.description: The code-host users assigned to the change request.

fields.name: requestedReviewers
fields.description: The code-host users from whom a review is currently requested.

fields.name: requestedTeams
fields.description: The code-host teams whose review is currently requested.

fields.name: labels
fields.description: The change request's labels.

fields.name: headRef
fields.description: The name of the branch containing the changes.

fields.name: baseRef
fields.description: The name of the branch into which the changes would be merged.

fields.name: headOID
fields.description: The current head commit of the change request.

fields.name: baseOID
fields.description: The base commit of the change request when it was last synchronized.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: When the change request was created on the code host.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: When the change request was last updated on the code host.

fields.name: syncedAt
fields.description: When Sourcegraph last synchronized the change request.

fields.name: closedAt
fields.description:
When the change request was closed on the code host, or null if it was not
closed.

fields.name: mergedAt
fields.description: When the change request was merged, or null if it was not merged.

fields.name: diffStat
fields.description:
The code host's diff statistics as of the last synchronization, or null if
the code host did not report them. Currently supports GitHub.

fields.name: fileGrouping
fields.description:
File review priorities for the current synchronized revision. Read-only:
querying this field never schedules analysis. Null if no job exists or
the repository is not available to the viewer.

fields.name: signals
fields.description:
Signals computed for the current synchronized head, such as security scan
results. Read-only: querying this field never schedules analysis. Empty if
none were computed or the repository is not available to the viewer.

fields.name: viewerIsAuthor
fields.description: Whether the viewer is the author of this change request.

fields.name: stack
fields.description:
The stack containing the change request, or null if it is not part of a
stack. Currently supports GitHub stacked pull requests.

fields.name: reviewStatus
fields.description:
The code host's overall review status as of the last synchronization, or
null if the code host reports none, such as a GitHub pull request without
approving or change-requesting reviews whose base branch does not require
reviews. Currently supports GitHub.

fields.name: reviews
fields.description:
The latest review of each reviewer who approved or requested changes, as of
the last synchronization, including reviewers whose review does not count
toward the review status. Excludes comment-only and dismissed reviews.
Currently supports GitHub, up to 100 reviewers.

fields.name: viewerReports
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: The viewer's review reports for this change request, for any
head, newest first. At most 50. Empty if the repository is not available to
the viewer.

fields.name: reviewThreads
fields.description:
The threads of inline comments on the change request's diff as of the last
synchronization, ordered by path and line. Empty if the repository is not
available to the viewer. Currently supports GitHub, up to 100 comments per
thread.

fields.name: chatMessages
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Messages in the change request's chat. Chat messages are
stored only in Sourcegraph, not posted to the code host. Empty if the
repository is not available to the viewer.

args.name: first
args.description:
Returns the first n messages. Must be between 1 and 100, and cannot be
combined with last.

args.name: after
args.description: Opaque cursor from pageInfo.endCursor. Returns messages after it.

args.name: last
args.description:
Returns the last n messages, such as the most recent ones. Must be
between 1 and 100, and cannot be combined with first.

args.name: before
args.description: Opaque cursor from pageInfo.startCursor. Returns messages before it.

types.name: ChangeRequestBooleanComparator
types.description: Compares a boolean. Set at most one field.

inputFields.name: eq
inputFields.description: Equals the given value.

inputFields.name: neq
inputFields.description: Does not equal the given value.

types.name: ChangeRequestChatMessage
types.description: EXPERIMENTAL: A message in a change request's chat.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique ID of the message.

fields.name: author
fields.description: The user who sent the message, or null if they were deleted.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
The message text, in Markdown. Clients must sanitize it before rendering
it as HTML.

fields.name: headOID
fields.description: The change request's head when the message was sent.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: When the message was sent.

fields.name: viewerCanDelete
fields.description: Whether the viewer can delete the message. Only its author can.

types.name: ChangeRequestChatMessageConnection
types.description:
A page of chat messages. Nodes are always oldest first, whether paging forward
or backward.

fields.name: nodes
fields.description: The messages in this page.

fields.name: pageInfo
fields.description: Pagination information.

types.name: ChangeRequestCodeHostAccountInput
types.description: An account on a code host, identified by its login.

inputFields.name: codeHostURL
inputFields.description: The code host's base URL, ignoring a trailing slash.

inputFields.name: login
inputFields.description:
The account's case-insensitive login on the code host, as stored when the
change request was last synchronized.

types.name: ChangeRequestConnection
types.description:
A page of change requests. Nodes are always newest first, whether paging
forward or backward.

fields.name: nodes
fields.description: The change requests in this page.

fields.name: pageInfo
fields.description: Pagination information.

types.name: ChangeRequestDateComparator
types.description: Compares a date. Together, gte and lt select a half-open range.

inputFields.name: gte
inputFields.description: Is at or after the given time.

inputFields.name: lt
inputFields.description: Is before the given time.

types.name: ChangeRequestDiffStat
types.description: Diff statistics for a change request, as reported by its code host.

fields.name: added
fields.description: Number of lines added.

fields.name: deleted
fields.description: Number of lines deleted.

fields.name: changedFiles
fields.description: Number of files changed.

types.name: ChangeRequestFileCategory
types.description: Suggested review attention, not a guarantee of correctness or safety.

types.name: ChangeRequestFileGroup
types.description: A group of changed files with the same suggested level of review attention.

fields.name: category
fields.description: Suggested review attention.

fields.name: files
fields.description: Existing comparison file objects, in grouping order.

types.name: ChangeRequestFileGrouping
types.description: Analysis of an immutable PR comparison, using the merge base like GitHub's PR diff.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Generation state. SKIPPED means the repository was absent from Sourcegraph.

fields.name: diffBaseOID
fields.description: The resolved merge base, or null before comparison preparation.

fields.name: headOID
fields.description: The PR head being analyzed.

fields.name: groups
fields.description:
Review, skim, and skip, in that order. Empty until a complete result exists.
Files are filtered by the viewer's current permissions.

types.name: ChangeRequestFileGroupingStatus
types.description: The lifecycle of file grouping generation. Retryable failures remain QUEUED.

types.name: ChangeRequestFilter
types.description:
Filters for synchronized change requests. All supplied filters and all
comparator fields within a filter are combined. Omitted filters and
comparator fields are unrestricted.

inputFields.name: state
inputFields.description: The change request's state.

inputFields.name: draft
inputFields.description: Whether the change request is a draft.

inputFields.name: author
inputFields.description:
The author. A Sourcegraph user matches linked code-host accounts or verified
emails in the stored payload. A code-host account matches its login on that
code host. Currently supports GitHub, so nin matches all change requests on
other code hosts.

inputFields.name: requestedReviewers
inputFields.description:
The reviewers from whom a review is currently requested. Does not imply a
state or draft filter.

A Sourcegraph user includes direct and team requests. Direct requests match
a linked code-host account or verified email in the stored payload. Team
requests require a linked GitHub account and app-synchronized membership
from the last 30 minutes, so none still matches team requests whose
membership is stale. Membership is refreshed periodically using Review
GitHub App installations with Organization members: read permission.

A code-host account matches only direct requests for its login on that code
host. Currently supports GitHub.

inputFields.name: repository
inputFields.description: The repository name on the code host, such as owner/name.

inputFields.name: repositoryArchived
inputFields.description:
Whether the repository is archived on the code host. Omit to include
change requests of both archived and active repositories.

inputFields.name: codeHostURL
inputFields.description: The code-host base URL. Equality ignores a trailing slash.

inputFields.name: createdAt
inputFields.description: When the change request was created on the code host.

inputFields.name: updatedAt
inputFields.description: When the change request was last updated on the code host.

inputFields.name: mergedAt
inputFields.description:
When the change request was merged. Excludes change requests that were not
merged.

inputFields.name: closedAt
inputFields.description:
When the change request was closed on the code host. Excludes change
requests that were not closed. Code hosts such as GitHub also report a close
time for merged change requests.

inputFields.name: id
inputFields.description:
The change request's ID, such as to exclude change requests that a user
dismissed.

types.name: ChangeRequestIDComparator
types.description: Compares a change request's ID. Lists contain at most 500 IDs.

inputFields.name: nin
inputFields.description: Is none of the given change requests.

types.name: ChangeRequestMergeMethod
types.description:
An available code-host-specific merge option. Clients must not infer semantics
from the ID or assume all code hosts offer the same strategies.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Opaque method identifier to send to mergeChangeRequest.

fields.name: label
fields.description: User-facing description of this method's behavior on the code host.

types.name: ChangeRequestMergeOptions
types.description: Live merge methods available to the viewer for a specific changeset head.

fields.name: state
fields.description:
The host's current merge readiness. A failed lookup returns a GraphQL error,
not BLOCKED. READY is advisory; merging rechecks readiness and the head.

fields.name: methods
fields.description: Allowed methods, in preferred order. Empty when merging is blocked.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Why merging is blocked, or an empty string when it is available.

types.name: ChangeRequestMergeReadiness
types.description: Merge readiness, distinct from individual CI check results.

enumValues.name: READY
enumValues.description: The viewer can attempt a supported merge method.

enumValues.name: BLOCKED
enumValues.description: A known condition or code-host rule prevents merging.

enumValues.name: CHECKING
enumValues.description: The code host is still calculating readiness.

enumValues.name: UNSUPPORTED
enumValues.description: Merge on the code host; in-app merging is unsupported.

types.name: ChangeRequestParticipantCollectionComparator
types.description:
Compares a list of change request participants. Lists contain at most 20
participants.

inputFields.name: some
inputFields.description: Any of the given participants is in the list. An empty list is unrestricted.

inputFields.name: none
inputFields.description: None of the given participants is in the list.

types.name: ChangeRequestParticipantComparator
types.description:
Compares a single change request participant. Lists contain at most 20
participants.

inputFields.name: in
inputFields.description: Is any of the given participants. An empty list is unrestricted.

inputFields.name: nin
inputFields.description: Is none of the given participants.

types.name: ChangeRequestParticipantInput
types.description:
A change request participant used in filters. Set exactly one field. A
Sourcegraph user without linked accounts or verified emails matches nothing
for in and some, and excludes nothing for nin and none.

inputFields.name: user
inputFields.description: The ID of a Sourcegraph user.

inputFields.name: codeHostAccount
inputFields.description: A code-host account, which does not need to be linked to a Sourcegraph user.

types.name: ChangeRequestReport
types.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: A review report: a structured document an agent wrote about one
revision of a change request, following a viewer's prompt.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique ID of the report.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: The prompt the report was requested with.

fields.name: effort
fields.description: The effort the report was requested with.

fields.name: state
fields.description: Generation state.

fields.name: partial
fields.description:
Whether a COMPLETED report ended before the agent finished, for example
because it used up its budget. The document contains what it produced.

fields.name: failureMessage
fields.description: Why generation failed, or null unless FAILED.

fields.name: diffBaseOID
fields.description:
The merge base the report compares against, or null before generation
resolved it. Lines on the base side of the document refer to this revision.

fields.name: headOID
fields.description:
The change request head the report describes. Lines on the head side of the
document refer to this revision.

fields.name: document
fields.description:
The report document as JSON, or null until the agent has produced an
outline. Its format is versioned by its version field; see the client's
report spec for the shape. Updated while PROCESSING.

fields.name: creator
fields.description: The user who requested the report, or null if they were deleted.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: When the report was requested.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: When the report or its document last changed.

types.name: ChangeRequestReportEffort
types.description:
How much investigation a report's agent may do. More effort takes longer and
reads more context.

enumValues.name: QUICK
enumValues.description: Reads only the diff. Fastest.

enumValues.name: STANDARD
enumValues.description: Reads the diff and surrounding files.

enumValues.name: DEEP
enumValues.description: Investigates further, with a larger budget.

types.name: ChangeRequestReportState
types.description: The lifecycle of a review report.

enumValues.name: QUEUED
enumValues.description: Waiting for a worker.

enumValues.name: PROCESSING
enumValues.description: The agent is working; the document may be partially filled in.

enumValues.name: COMPLETED
enumValues.description: Generation ended with a document. See partial.

enumValues.name: FAILED
enumValues.description: Generation ended without a usable document. See failureMessage.

types.name: ChangeRequestReview
types.description:
A reviewer's latest review of a change request that approved it or requested
changes.

fields.name: reviewer
fields.description: The code-host user who submitted the review.

fields.name: state
fields.description: The review's verdict.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
The review's summary text as raw, unsanitized code-host markup, or empty
if the reviewer wrote none. Excludes inline comments. Clients must sanitize
it before rendering it as HTML.

fields.name: commitOID
fields.description:
The commit that was reviewed, or null if it is unknown. A commit other than
the change request's headOID means the review predates the latest changes.

fields.name: submittedAt
fields.description: When the review was submitted.

types.name: ChangeRequestReviewAction
types.description: An action that can be submitted as part of a change-request review.

types.name: ChangeRequestReviewComment
types.description: A comment of a change request review thread.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique ID of the comment.

fields.name: author
fields.description:
The code-host user who wrote the comment, or null if the account was
deleted.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
The comment as raw, unsanitized code-host markup. Clients must sanitize it
before rendering it as HTML.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The comment's URL on the code host.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: When the comment was created on the code host.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: When the comment was last updated on the code host.

types.name: ChangeRequestReviewCommentPayload
types.description: The result of posting a change request review comment.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The outcome of posting the comment.

fields.name: currentHeadOID
fields.description: The latest head commit when status is HEAD_CHANGED.

fields.name: threadID
fields.description: The ID of the thread containing the comment when status is SUCCESS.

fields.name: comment
fields.description:
The posted comment when status is SUCCESS. It appears in the change
request's reviewThreads after the next synchronization.

types.name: ChangeRequestReviewDraftThread
types.description: A thread of inline comments that is started as part of a review.

inputFields.name: path
inputFields.description: The path of the commented file in the diff.

inputFields.name: startSide
inputFields.description: The side containing the first line.

inputFields.name: startLine
inputFields.description: The first line, inclusive, in the file on startSide.

inputFields.name: endSide
inputFields.description: The side containing the last line.

inputFields.name: endLine
inputFields.description: The last line, inclusive, in the file on endSide.

inputFields.name: body
inputFields.description: The comment as code-host markup.

types.name: ChangeRequestReviewState
types.description: The verdict of a change-request review.

enumValues.name: APPROVED
enumValues.description: The reviewer approved the change request.

enumValues.name: CHANGES_REQUESTED
enumValues.description: The reviewer requested changes.

types.name: ChangeRequestReviewStatus
types.description: The overall review status of a change request, as reported by its code host.

enumValues.name: APPROVED
enumValues.description:
The change request is approved, including any approvals its code host
requires.

enumValues.name: CHANGES_REQUESTED
enumValues.description: A reviewer requested changes.

enumValues.name: REVIEW_REQUIRED
enumValues.description: The code host requires more approving reviews.

types.name: ChangeRequestReviewThread
types.description:
A thread of inline comments on a change request's diff, as reported by its
code host.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique ID of the thread. It is stable across synchronizations.

fields.name: path
fields.description: The path of the commented file in the diff.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description:
The thread's location in the diff between the change request's baseOID and
headOID, or null if the thread is outdated or not attached to lines.

fields.name: isResolved
fields.description: Whether the thread was resolved on the code host.

fields.name: isOutdated
fields.description: Whether the commented lines changed since the thread was started.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The thread's URL on the code host.

fields.name: comments
fields.description: The thread's comments, oldest first. The first comment started the thread.

types.name: ChangeRequestSecurityFinding
types.description: A security scan finding.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: What the finding is about.

fields.name: severity
fields.description: The finding's severity.

fields.name: rule
fields.description: The rule that produced the finding.

fields.name: ruleURL
fields.description: A link to the rule's documentation, if available.

fields.name: message
fields.description: The scan service's explanation.

fields.name: path
fields.description: The file path in the scanned head.

fields.name: line
fields.description: The first line of the finding, starting at 1.

fields.name: endLine
fields.description: The last line of the finding, starting at 1.

types.name: ChangeRequestSecurityFindingKind
types.description: The category of a security finding.

enumValues.name: CODE
enumValues.description: A vulnerability or weakness in the code.

enumValues.name: SUPPLY_CHAIN
enumValues.description: A vulnerable dependency.

enumValues.name: SECRETS
enumValues.description: A hardcoded secret.

types.name: ChangeRequestSecurityFindingSeverity
types.description: The severity of a security finding.

types.name: ChangeRequestSecurityScanSignal
types.description: A security scan service's results for a change request's head.

fields.name: headOID
fields.description: The head the signal was computed for.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: When the signal was last computed.

fields.name: provider
fields.description: The scan service's name, such as Semgrep.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The state of the head's scan.

fields.name: error
fields.description: Why Sourcegraph couldn't get results, for the ERROR status.

fields.name: scanURL
fields.description: A link to the scan on the scan service, or null if there is no scan.

fields.name: findings
fields.description:
Findings that still need attention, most severe first. Empty unless the
status is COMPLETED. Filtered by the viewer's current permissions.

fields.name: findingsTruncated
fields.description: Whether the scan service reported more findings than are listed.

types.name: ChangeRequestSecurityScanStatus
types.description: The state of a change request head's security scan.

enumValues.name: PENDING
enumValues.description:
The scan service has not finished scanning the head. Sourcegraph checks
again every few minutes for up to 6 hours.

enumValues.name: COMPLETED
enumValues.description: The scan completed.

enumValues.name: FAILED
enumValues.description: The scan did not complete.

enumValues.name: NOT_SCANNED
enumValues.description:
The scan service does not scan the repository, or no scan of the head
finished within 6 hours.

enumValues.name: ERROR
enumValues.description:
Sourcegraph couldn't get results from the scan service. Sourcegraph retries
every few minutes for up to 6 hours.

types.name: ChangeRequestSignal
types.description: A result computed for a change request's head.

fields.name: headOID
fields.description: The head the signal was computed for.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: When the signal was last computed.

types.name: ChangeRequestStack
types.description:
An ordered chain of change requests in one repository, where each change
request is based on the one below it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique ID of the stack.

fields.name: changeRequests
fields.description:
The synchronized members of the stack from the bottom, which merges first,
to the top. Includes merged and closed members and ignores list filters.

types.name: ChangeRequestState
types.description: The state of a change request.

enumValues.name: OPEN
enumValues.description: The change request is open.

enumValues.name: CLOSED
enumValues.description: The change request was closed without being merged.

enumValues.name: MERGED
enumValues.description: The change request was merged.

enumValues.name: UNKNOWN
enumValues.description: The code host reported a state that Sourcegraph does not recognize.

types.name: ChangeRequestStateComparator
types.description: Compares a change request's state.

inputFields.name: eq
inputFields.description: Equals the given state.

inputFields.name: neq
inputFields.description: Does not equal the given state.

inputFields.name: in
inputFields.description: Is any of the given states. An empty list is unrestricted.

inputFields.name: nin
inputFields.description: Is none of the given states.

types.name: ChangeRequestStringComparator
types.description: Compares a string, ignoring case. Empty values are unrestricted.

inputFields.name: eq
inputFields.description: Equals the given value.

inputFields.name: neq
inputFields.description: Does not equal the given value.

inputFields.name: contains
inputFields.description: Contains the given value as a literal substring.

inputFields.name: notContains
inputFields.description: Does not contain the given value as a literal substring.

types.name: ChangeRequestViewer
types.description: A user who is looking at, or recently looked at, a change request.

fields.name: user
fields.description: The user.

fields.name: active
fields.description: Whether any of the user's sessions is looking at the change request now.

fields.name: reviewing
fields.description:
Whether any of the user's sessions is writing a review of the change
request now.

fields.name: lastViewedAt
fields.description: When the user last looked at the change request.

types.name: ChangedFile
types.description: A file that was changed in a comparison.

fields.name: path
fields.description: The path of the file.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The status of the change.

fields.name: file
fields.description: The file object. For deletions, this is the old file. For all other changes, this is the new file.

fields.name: srcOID
fields.description: The source blob OID. Null if the file was added in this comparison.

fields.name: dstOID
fields.description: The destination blob OID. Null if the file was deleted in this comparison.

fields.name: gitAttributes
fields.description:
The requested Git attributes associated with this file.

Attributes are read from the head revision of the comparison, or from the
base revision for deleted files. They come from the .gitattributes files at
that revision and from repository-level attributes managed by the server.

At least one and at most 16 names must be requested. Names must consist of
ASCII letters, digits, '-', '.', and '_', and must not start with '-'.
Duplicate names are ignored. Unspecified attributes are omitted, and the
remaining attributes are returned in name order.

fields.name: viewerHasViewed
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Whether the viewing user has marked this file as reviewed
for the current (base, head) comparison. Automatically becomes false
again if the file's src or dst blob OID has changed since it was marked.

types.name: ChangedFileConnection
types.description: A list of changed files in a comparison.

fields.name: nodes
fields.description: The list of changed files.

fields.name: totalCount
fields.description: The total count of changed files.

fields.name: pageInfo
fields.description: Pagination information.

types.name: ChangedFileStatus
types.description: The type of change for a file.

enumValues.name: ADDED
enumValues.description: The file was added.

enumValues.name: MODIFIED
enumValues.description: The file contents were modified.

enumValues.name: DELETED
enumValues.description: The file was deleted.

enumValues.name: TYPE_CHANGED
enumValues.description:
Git reported a type change (`T` in `git diff-tree --name-status`), meaning the object
type changed at the same path (for example, regular file to symlink, symlink to regular
file, or file to submodule).

types.name: ChangedFileViewedRef
types.description:
Identity of a single file within a diff: canonical path plus the src and dst
blob OIDs that anchor the viewed state to a specific content snapshot. For
markChangedFilesAsUnviewed, srcOID and dstOID are ignored — a delete only
matches on path.

inputFields.name: path
inputFields.description: The canonical path of the file (post-image path, or pre-image if deleted).

inputFields.name: srcOID
inputFields.description:
The source (pre-image) blob OID from ChangedFile.srcOID, or null if the
file was added in this diff.

inputFields.name: dstOID
inputFields.description:
The destination (post-image) blob OID from ChangedFile.dstOID, or null if
the file was deleted in this diff.

types.name: CheckMirrorRepositoryConnectionResult
types.description: The result for Mutation.checkMirrorRepositoryConnection.

fields.name: error
fields.description:
The error message encountered during the update operation, if any. If null, then
the connection check succeeded.

types.name: ChunkMatch
types.description: A set of matched ranges contained in a chunk of contiguous lines.

fields.name: content
fields.description: The contiguous set of full lines which contain the matches in ranges.

fields.name: contentStart
fields.description: The location of the beginning of content.

fields.name: ranges
fields.description: The set of ranges within the content that matched the search query.

fields.name: bestLineMatch

fields.description: Coarse description of the data source for this code graph data.

fields.description:
The commit associated with this code graph data.

In general, this will be an ancestor of the commit at which code
graph data was requested, as code graph data may not be available
at the exact commit for the blob.

fields.name: toolInfo
fields.description:
Information about the tool which generated this code graph data.

This information may be missing if the tool itself did not specify
the information in the generated SCIP index. This field is always
available for all Sourcegraph-maintained indexers.

fields.name: occurrences
fields.description:
Occurrences are guaranteed to be sorted by range based on
(start.line, start.character, end.line, end.character) as a 4-tuple.
It is possible for there to be:
- Multiple occurrences for the same exact source range.
- Occurrences which intersect without one containing the other.
- Occurrences which span across multiple lines.

At the moment, using higher values of 'first:' should not cause
significantly worst performance.

As an example, for a large C++ codebase, here are the percentiles
for number of occurrences per document.

| Percentile | Occurrences count |
|       50   |               241 |
|       90   |              2443 |
|       95   |              4554 |
|       99   |             15869 |
|       99.9 |             94465 |
|      100   |            707850 |

fields.name: relationships
fields.description:
Relationships represents additional metadata about how symbols are related
to each other.

At the moment, this will only return information relationships defined within
the same file.

E.g. if Dog.java has a class Dog which subclasses Animal defined in
Animal.java then the IS_IMPLEMENTATION relationship defined on Dog will
be returned when accessing relationships(..) for Dog.java.

However, this relationship will not show up when accessing relationships(..)
for Animal.java.

types.name: CompendiaMutation
types.description: Mutations on compendia.

fields.name: create
fields.description:
Enqueue a new compendium for a free-text request. Returns immediately with
state QUEUED; poll the compendium until COMPLETED.

fields.name: regenerate
fields.description:
Regenerate a compendium in place. The previous edition is given to the generator
so the new one keeps its structure where still accurate; chapters whose cited
code did not change are carried over as they are. With rewrite, every chapter
is written afresh instead, with the previous edition as a guide to scope only:
for when the generator itself changed. A no-op while the compendium is already
generating.

fields.name: regenerateAll
fields.description:
Regenerate every compendium with an edition that the viewer may see, as
regenerate does for one, rewrite included: for when the generator itself
changed. Each is attributed to the viewer and generated as them.
Compendia already generating are left as they are. Administrators only.
Returns how many compendia were queued.

fields.name: revise
fields.description:
Rewrite some chapters of the current edition against the code at head
without re-planning the article; the edition number is kept. With no
chapters given, the chapters the last freshness check found stale are
revised, along with every chapter that cites code the check saw change.
A no-op while the compendium is already generating.

fields.name: requestDiagram
fields.description:
Ask for an additional diagram of a compendium, e.g. "the request lifecycle".
Returns immediately with state QUEUED; poll the compendium's requestedDiagrams.

fields.name: addNote
fields.description:
Leave a note for the generator: what the next edition should do
differently. Notes never appear in the compendium; before the next
regeneration they are distilled into the compendium's standing directions.

fields.name: deleteNote
fields.description:
Remove a note. Removing an applied note does not undo its effect on the
directions.

fields.name: attachThread
fields.description:
Bind a Deep Search conversation the viewer owns to the part of a
compendium it was asked about, so it is shown again next to that part.
Binding the same conversation twice is a no-op.

fields.name: setSlug
fields.description: Name the compendium's URL: /compendium/{slug}.

fields.name: setAutoRefresh
fields.description:
Opt the compendium into, or out of, being kept up to date automatically:
once its edition has drifted from the code it cites and the drift has
settled, the stale chapters are revised, or a new edition written when
the code was reorganized, without anyone asking.

fields.name: delete
fields.description:
Delete a compendium with every edition, diagram, note and conversation
binding it has. An edition in the works is abandoned.

types.name: Compendium
types.description:
An AI-written long-form article walking the reader through part of a
codebase, with embedded code excerpts and architecture diagrams.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The GraphQL ID.

fields.name: publicID
fields.description: The stable, non-enumerable identifier the URL uses when there is no slug.

fields.name: slug
fields.description: The share name the URL uses, if one is set.

fields.name: request
fields.description: The free-text request the compendium answers.

fields.name: state
fields.description: Where the compendium is in its generation.

fields.name: edition
fields.description: How many editions have been generated. 0 until the first completes.

fields.name: failureMessage
fields.description:
Why the last generation failed. Only set when state is FAILED, and only
for viewers who may request another edition.

fields.name: creator
fields.description: The user who requested the compendium, if still present.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: When the compendium was requested.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: When the compendium or its state last changed.

fields.name: changedAt
fields.description:
When the compendium last changed in a way a reader could see: it was
requeued, begun or finished, an edition or revision was stored, its
directions or auto-refresh setting changed, or a diagram was asked for,
begun or finished. Unlike updatedAt it covers the diagrams, so an open
page compares it with CompendiaQuery.status to learn when to reload.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The compendium's URL on this instance.

fields.name: backdropURL
fields.description:
The decorative sketch generated on creation, if available and visible to the viewer.
Served through an access-checked image URL.

fields.name: title
fields.description:
The headline. Null until an edition has been generated; while a
regeneration runs the previous edition stays visible.

fields.name: deck
fields.description: The standfirst under the headline.

fields.name: lede
fields.description: The opening section in Markdown.

fields.name: repositories
fields.description: The repositories the article cites, most important first.

fields.name: chapters
fields.description: The chapters of the current edition, in reading order.

fields.name: history
fields.description:
The chronicle: how the subsystem came to be, told through the commits
that shaped it. Null when the historian could not compile one for this
edition.

fields.name: diagrams
fields.description:
The diagrams drawn as part of the article. The first is the overview;
others belong to a chapter (see CompendiumDiagram.chapterID).

fields.name: requestedDiagrams
fields.description:
Diagrams readers asked for after the article was written. A request not
yet drawn is listed only for its requester and administrators.

fields.name: generatedAt
fields.description: When the current edition was written.

fields.name: threads
fields.description: Deep Search conversations readers started from this compendium.

fields.name: directions
fields.description:
The standing directions distilled from the editor's notes, in Markdown;
empty until a note has been applied. Every agent that writes an edition
is given them. Empty for viewers who may not write: the notes may name
code the compendium does not cite.

fields.name: notes
fields.description:
The editor's notes for the generator, oldest first. Empty for viewers who
may not write: the notes and their sketches may name code the compendium
does not cite.

fields.name: revisions
fields.description:
The commits the edition is pinned to: for each cited repository, where
its head was when the edition was written. Excerpts render at these
commits. Empty for editions written before pinning existed.

fields.name: freshness
fields.description:
What the last freshness check found, or null if the edition has not been
checked since it changed.

fields.name: revisedAt
fields.description:
When chapters of this edition were last revised against newer code
without a new edition, and which.

fields.name: revisedChapters
fields.description: The ids of the chapters the last revision rewrote.

fields.name: carriedChapters
fields.description:
The chapters this edition kept from the previous one without rewriting
them, because the plan kept them and nothing they cite changed.

fields.name: revisingChapters
fields.description: The chapters a queued or running revision is rewriting.

fields.name: autoRefresh
fields.description:
Whether the compendium is kept up to date automatically: once its
edition has drifted from the code it cites and the drift has settled,
the remedy the freshness check recommends is carried out without anyone
asking.

fields.name: related
fields.description:
Other compendia the edition points readers to, in the order recorded;
only those the viewer may read.

fields.name: citedBy
fields.description:
Compendia whose current edition points at this one and are not already
among related; only those the viewer may read, newest first.

fields.name: linked
suggestions
fields.description:
Compendia the edition recommends be commissioned. Empty unless the
viewer may create compendia.

fields.name: editions
fields.description:
The editions the compendium has had, newest first, the current one
among them. Empty unless the viewer may request editions.

args.name: first
args.description: Return the first n editions. Must be between 1 and 200; defaults to 50.

args.name: after
args.description: Opaque cursor from pageInfo.endCursor. Returns the editions after it.

fields.name: storedEdition
fields.description:
One of the compendium's editions by ID, or the newest when no ID is
given. Null when the compendium has no such edition, and unless the
viewer may request editions.

toggle its tools, and delete it.

fields.description:
Whether the user can use the connector. Always true for connectors with
shared credentials. For connectors with per-user authorization, whether the
user has authorized them.

The user is the one whose connectors User.connectors lists, and the current
user otherwise. The same applies to authorizationExpired and
disabledAgents.

fields.name: authorizationExpired
fields.description:
Whether the user authorized this connector, but the authorization expired
or was revoked, so they have to authorize it again.

fields.name: disabledAgents

fields.name: authorizeURL
fields.description:
The URL that starts the OAuth authorization flow for the current user. Null
unless the connector uses OAuth.

fields.name: oauthClientID
fields.description:
The manually registered OAuth client ID. Null for dynamically registered
clients and connectors without OAuth.

fields.name: oauthRedirectURL
fields.description:
The OAuth redirect URL the connector's client was registered with. Null
unless the connector uses OAuth.

fields.name: oauthRedirectURLOutdated
fields.description:
Whether the instance's external URL changed since the OAuth client was
registered, so users cannot connect until the connector is updated.

fields.name: headerNames
fields.description:
The names of the custom headers. Their values are secret. Empty unless the
current user can manage the connector.

fields.name: tools
fields.description: The tools of the server, as last listed.

fields.name: toolsUpdatedAt
fields.description:
When the tools were last listed. Null for connectors with per-user
authorization that nobody authorized yet.

fields.name: toolsRefreshError
fields.description:
The error of the last failed attempt to list the tools, unless a later
attempt succeeded. Null unless the current user can manage the connector.

fields.name: toolsRefreshFailedAt
fields.description: When listing the tools last failed.

fields.name: credentialsRejectedAt
fields.description:
When the server rejected the connector's shared credentials. Agents can't
use the connector until the credentials are updated or the server accepts
them again.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: When the connector was added.

fields.description:
The number of queries belonging to the series with errored status. Errored is a transient state representing a retryable error that has not
yet exceeded the max retry count. This count only represents the queries that have yet to be pruned by the background maintenance workers.

fields.name: completed

The number of queries belonging to the series that are successfully completed.
This count only represents the queries that have yet to be pruned by the background maintenance workers.

fields.name: processing

This count only represents the queries that have yet to be pruned by the background maintenance workers.

fields.name: failed
fields.description:
The number of queries belonging to the series that are terminally failed. These have either been marked as non-retryable or exceeded
the max retry limit. This count only represents the queries that have yet to be pruned by the background maintenance workers.

This count only represents the queries that have yet to be pruned by the background maintenance workers.

types.name: InsightSeriesStatus
types.description: Status indicators for a specific series of insight data.

fields.name: totalPoints
fields.description:
The total number of points stored for this series, at the finest level
(e.g. per repository, or per-repository-per-language) Has no strict relation
to the data points shown in the web UI or returned by `points()`, because those
are aggregated and this number _can_ report some duplicates points which get
stored but removed at query time for the web UI.

Why its useful: an insight may look like "it is doing nothing" but in reality
this number will be increasing by e.g. several thousands of points rapidly.

fields.name: pendingJobs
fields.description:
The total number of jobs currently pending to add new data points for this series.

Each job may create multiple data points (e.g. a job may create one data point per
repo, or language, etc.) This number will go up and down over time until all work
is completed (discovering work takes almost as long as doing the work.)

Why its useful: signals "amount of work still to be done."

fields.name: completedJobs
fields.description:
The total number of jobs completed for this series. Note that since pendingJobs will
go up/down over time, you CANNOT divide these two numbers to get a percentage as it
would be nonsense ("it says 90% complete but has been like that for a really long
time!").

Does not include 'failedJobs'.

Why its useful: gives an indication of "how much work has been done?"

fields.name: failedJobs
fields.description:
The total number of jobs that were tried multiple times and outright failed. They will
not be retried again, and indicates the series has incomplete data.

Use ((failedJobs / completedJobs) * 100.0) to get an approximate percentage of how
much data the series data may be missing (e.g. ((30 / 150)*100.0) == 20% of the series
data is incomplete (rough approximation, not precise).

Why its useful: signals if there are problems, and how severe they are.

fields.name: backfillQueuedAt
fields.description:
The time that the insight series completed a full iteration and queued up records for processing. This can
effectively be used as a status that the insight is still processing if returned null.

fields.name: isLoadingData
fields.description: Indicates if the series is currently loading additional data

fields.name: incompleteDatapoints
fields.description: Data points that are flagged terminally incomplete for this series.

HEURISTIC (default) optimizes only what's needed based on Git's assessment.

fields.name: createUser
fields.description:
Creates a new user account.

Only site admins may perform this mutation.

args.name: username
args.description: The new user's username.

args.name: email
args.description: The new user's optional email address. If given, it must be verified by the user.

args.name: verifiedEmail
args.description:
Whether or not to mark the provided email address as verified. If unset or set to
true, then the email address is immediately marked as verified - otherwise, the
email may be marked as unverified if SMTP and password resets are enabled.

args.name: isServiceAccount
args.description:
Whether this is a service account for automation rather than a regular user account.
Service accounts don't have an email or password.

fields.name: randomizeUserPassword
fields.description:
Randomize a user's password so that they need to reset it before they can sign in again.

Only site admins may perform this mutation.

fields.name: addUserEmail
fields.description:
Adds an email address to the user's account. The email address will be marked as unverified until the user
has followed the email verification process.

Only the user and site admins may perform this mutation.

fields.name: removeUserEmail
fields.description:
Removes an email address from the user's account.

Only the user and site admins may perform this mutation.

fields.name: setUserEmailPrimary
fields.description:
Set an email address as the user's primary.

Only the user and site admins may perform this mutation. Check user.viewerCanChangePrimaryEmail
for permission and other update inhibitors.

fields.name: setUserEmailVerified
fields.description:
Manually set the verification status of a user's email, without going through the normal verification process
(of clicking on a link in the email with a verification code).

Only site admins may perform this mutation.

fields.name: resendVerificationEmail
fields.description:
Resend a verification email, no op if the email is already verified.

Only the user and site admins may perform this mutation.

fields.name: deleteUser
fields.description:
Deletes a user account. Only site admins may perform this mutation.

If hard == true, a hard delete is performed. By default, deletes are
'soft deletes' and could theoretically be undone with manual DB commands.
If a hard delete is performed, the data is truly removed from the
database and deletion can NEVER be undone.

Data that is deleted as part of this operation:

- All user data (access tokens, email addresses, external account info, survey responses, etc)
- Organization membership information (which organizations the user is a part of, any invitations created by or targeting the user).
- User, Organization, or Global settings authored by the user.

fields.name: deleteUsers
fields.description: Bulk "deleteUser" action.

fields.name: recoverUsers
fields.description: Bulk "recoverUser" action.

fields.name: updatePassword
fields.description: Updates the current user's password. The oldPassword arg must match the user's current password.

fields.name: createPassword
fields.description: Creates a password for the current user. It is only permitted if the user does not have a password and password authentication is enabled.

fields.name: setTosAccepted
fields.description:
Sets the user to accept the site's Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
If the ID is omitted, the current user is assumed.

Only the user or site admins may perform this mutation.

fields.name: createAccessToken
fields.description:
Creates an access token that grants the privileges of the specified user (referred to as the access token's
"subject" user after token creation). The result is the access token value, which the caller is responsible
for storing (it is not accessible by Sourcegraph after creation).

The supported scopes are:

- "user:all": Full control of all resources accessible to the user account.
- "site-admin:sudo": Ability to perform any action as any other user. (Only site admins may create tokens
  with this scope.)
- "mcp": Access to MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoints only. This is a limited scope that does not
  grant full API access.

DurationSeconds: If provided, the number of seconds until the token expires automatically.

Only the user or site admins may perform this mutation.

fields.name: deleteAccessToken
fields.description:
Deletes and immediately revokes the specified access token, specified by either its ID or by the token
itself.

Only site admins or the user who owns the token may perform this mutation.

fields.name: deleteExternalAccount
fields.description:
Deletes the association between an external account and its Sourcegraph user. It does NOT delete the external
account on the external service where it resides.

Only site admins or the user who is associated with the external account may perform this mutation.

fields.name: addExternalAccount
fields.description:
Adds an external account to the authenticated user's account. The service type and service ID
must correspond to a valid auth provider on the site. The account details must be a stringified
JSON object that contains valid credentials for the provided service type.

fields.name: inviteUserToOrganization
fields.description:
Invite the user with the given username to join the organization. The invited user account must already
exist.

Only site admins and any organization member may perform this mutation.

fields.name: respondToOrganizationInvitation
fields.description:
Accept or reject an existing organization invitation.

Only the recipient of the invitation may perform this mutation.

args.name: organizationInvitation
args.description: The organization invitation.

args.name: responseType
args.description: The response to the invitation.

fields.name: addUserToOrganization
fields.description:
Immediately add a user as a member to the organization, without sending an invitation email.

Only site admins may perform this mutation. Organization members may use the inviteUserToOrganization
mutation to invite users.

fields.name: removeUserFromOrganization
fields.description:
Removes a user as a member from an organization.

Only site admins and any member of the organization may perform this mutation.

fields.name: setMigrationDirection
fields.description:
Updates an out-of-band migration to run in a particular direction.

Applied in the forward direction, an out-of-band migration migrates data into a format that
is readable by newer Sourcegraph instances. This may be destructive or non-destructive process,
depending on the nature and implementation of the migration.

Applied in the reverse direction, an out-of-band migration ensures that data is moved back into
a format that is readable by the previous Sourcegraph instance. Recently introduced migrations
should be applied in reverse prior to downgrading the instance.

fields.name: upsertDockerRegistryCredential
fields.description:
Adds or updates a single container registry credential inside a
DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG executor secret. If the DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG executor
secret does not yet exist in the target namespace, it is created with the
supplied credential as its single entry.
Exactly one of (`username` + `password`) or `auth` must be supplied:
  - When `username` and `password` are supplied, the server encodes
    `base64(username:password)` and stores that as the credential.
  - When `auth` is supplied, it must already be a `base64(username:password)`
    string (e.g. taken from `docker login`'s `~/.docker/config.json`).
Only BATCHES scope is currently supported.
`namespace` selects which DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG secret to modify. It may be a
User ID or an Org ID. Non-admins may only target their own user namespace
or an org they belong to; site admins may target any namespace. When
`namespace` is omitted, the site-wide (global) DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG secret
is targeted; this is restricted to site admins.

args.name: registry
args.description: The container registry host (e.g. "index.docker.io" or "ghcr.io").

args.name: username
args.description: The username to authenticate to the registry as. Mutually exclusive with `auth`.

args.name: password
args.description: The password / token to authenticate to the registry with. Mutually exclusive with `auth`.

args.name: auth
args.description:
A pre-encoded `base64(username:password)` credential string. Mutually
exclusive with `username` / `password`.

args.name: namespace
args.description:
The namespace that owns the DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG secret. May be a User
ID or an Org ID. Non-admins may only target their own user namespace
or an org they belong to; site admins may target any namespace. When
omitted, the site-wide (global) secret is targeted; this is restricted
to site admins.

fields.name: deleteDockerRegistryCredential
fields.description:
Removes a single container registry credential from a DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG
executor secret. If the resulting auth config has no remaining entries,
the entire executor secret is deleted and null is returned.
Only BATCHES scope is currently supported.
See `upsertDockerRegistryCredential` for namespace selection rules.

args.name: registry
args.description: The container registry host whose credential should be removed.

args.name: namespace
args.description:
The namespace that owns the DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG secret. May be a User
ID or an Org ID. When omitted, the site-wide (global) secret is
targeted; this is restricted to site admins.

fields.name: deleteGitHubApp

authentication provider, will be deleted.
🚨 SECURITY: Requires site-admin or REPO_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission.

fields.name: refreshGitHubApp
fields.description:
Refresh a GitHub App. This fetches information about the GitHub app and updates all installations
associated with it.
🚨 SECURITY: Authorization depends on the App's kind. Site credential Apps require site-admin;
user credential Apps require site-admin or the creating user; all other Apps require site-admin
or REPO_MANAGEMENT#READ permission.

fields.name: createGitHubApp
fields.description:
Add an existing GitHub App. This uses the provided Client ID and Private Key to fetch the GitHub
App details from GitHub and store it in the database.
🚨 SECURITY: Requires site-admin or REPO_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission.

fields.name: addGitHubAppAuthProvider
fields.description:
Adds a GitHub App as an authentication provider in the site configuration.
This appends a new GitHub auth provider entry (using the app's clientID, clientSecret, and baseURL)
to the "auth.providers" list in site config. If a matching provider already exists, this is a no-op.
🚨 SECURITY: Requires site-admin or REPO_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission.

mutation will be revoked for the role.

fields.description:
Create a new IdP client. The secret will be returned and can never be accessed
again.

Requires IDP_CLIENTS#WRITE permission.

args.description: A descriptive name for the client. Will be shown to users.

args.name: description

A detailed description of what this client does and why it needs access.
Will be shown to users on consent screens.

args.name: redirectURIs
args.description: The list of permitted redirect URIs.

args.name: scopes
args.description: The list of scopes this client can request.

args.name: public
args.description:
Whether this is a public client.

Public clients don't need to present a client secret. This is suitable for
single-page applications, mobile apps, and CLI tools. The client supports
device flow authentication.

Private clients need to provide the client secret for authorization flows.
Suitable for server-side applications, internal services, and M2M use-cases.

This setting cannot be changed after creation.

args.name: maxSessionDurationSeconds
args.description:
The maximum duration, in seconds, that an OAuth session for this client may
live since the user's original authentication. When set, access and refresh
tokens stop working that long after the user authenticated, even if they
were recently issued or rotated, forcing the user to re-authenticate. Null
means no limit.

fields.name: updateIDPClient
fields.description:
Update an existing IdP client.

Requires IDP_CLIENTS#WRITE permission.

args.name: id
args.description: The ID of the client to update.

args.name: name
args.description: A descriptive name for the client. Will be shown to users.

args.name: description
args.description:
A detailed description of what this client does and why it needs access.
Will be shown to users on consent screens.

args.name: redirectURIs
args.description: The list of permitted redirect URIs.

args.name: scopes

args.name: maxSessionDurationSeconds

live since the user's original authentication. When set, access and refresh
tokens stop working that long after the user authenticated, even if they
were recently issued or rotated, forcing the user to re-authenticate. Null
removes the limit.

are no longer usable.

Requires IDP_CLIENTS#WRITE permission.

fields.description:
Revoke the UserConsentedIDPClient consent.
This will invalidate all access tokens and refresh tokens issued to this client
for the current user, and force a consent prompt for the next authorization flow.

Can only be called by the user who owns the consent, or a site-admin.

Create a new M2M (Machine-to-Machine) credential for a service account.
This creates an IdP client that can use client credentials flow to obtain
access tokens with the service account as the subject.

Requires IDP_CLIENTS#WRITE_IMPERSONATION permission.

args.name: scopes

This will delete the associated IdP client and invalidate all access tokens.

Requires IDP_CLIENTS#WRITE_IMPERSONATION permission.

fields.name: mergeChangeRequest
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Merges one changeset as the viewer's linked code-host account.
Rechecks readiness and atomically requires the displayed head to match.
Requires the same access as changeRequest. Does not bypass code-host rules.

fields.name: moveChangeRequestFile
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Moves one file to a review category for all viewers. Only
the author may edit; the synchronized base and head must still match.

fields.name: reportChangeRequestPresence
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Reports whether the viewer is looking at, and reviewing, a
change request in one browser session, and returns the users looking at it
or who looked at it in the last 4 hours: the viewer first, then those
looking at it, and the rest most recent first. Clients report active about
every 15 seconds while the page is visible, and inactive when it is hidden
or closed. A session stops counting 45 seconds after its last active report.

fields.name: createChangeRequestReport
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Requests a review report of the change request's current
synchronized head, shaped by the viewer's prompt. Generation is
asynchronous: the report starts QUEUED, and its document fills in as the
agent works. Poll changeRequestReport for progress.

fields.name: sendChangeRequestChatMessage
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Sends a message to the change request's chat as the viewer.
The message is stored only in Sourcegraph, not posted to the code host.

fields.name: deleteChangeRequestChatMessage
fields.description: EXPERIMENTAL: Deletes one of the viewer's own chat messages.

fields.name: submitChangeRequestReview
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Submits a review for a code-host change request. The initial
implementation supports GitHub pull requests only.

fields.name: addChangeRequestReviewThread
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Starts a thread of inline comments on a change request's
diff as the viewer's linked code-host account. The comment is posted
immediately. Currently supports GitHub.

fields.name: replyToChangeRequestReviewThread
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Replies to a thread of inline comments as the viewer's linked
code-host account. Currently supports GitHub.

fields.name: deleteChangeRequestReviewComment
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Deletes a comment of a change request review thread as the
viewer's linked code-host account, if the code host allows it. Currently
supports GitHub.

fields.name: connectReviewSemgrep
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Connects Semgrep to show security scan results on
changesets, replacing any existing connection. Requires the
INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission and the bacon feature flag.

fields.name: disconnectReviewSemgrep
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Disconnects Semgrep. Sourcegraph stops requesting scan
results; results already shown on changesets remain. Requires the
INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission and the bacon feature flag.

fields.name: compendia
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Mutations on compendia. Require the COMPENDIA#WRITE
permission.

fields.name: createConnector
fields.description:
Creates a connector after checking that Sourcegraph can talk to it. For
connectors with shared credentials, this lists the server's tools. For
OAuth connectors, this discovers the authorization server and registers
Sourcegraph as an OAuth client.

Personal connectors require the CONNECTORS#WRITE_USER permission. Other
connectors require the INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission.

fields.name: updateConnector
fields.description:
Updates a connector and checks connectivity like createConnector. Users
have to connect again if the server or OAuth client changes, for example
because the instance's external URL changed.

Requires the INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE permission, or owning the
personal connector and the CONNECTORS#WRITE_USER permission, like all
mutations that manage a connector.

fields.name: deleteConnector
fields.description: Deletes a connector and all user authorizations for it.

fields.name: setConnectorToolsEnabled
fields.description:
Enables or disables tools of a connector. Tools are enabled by default,
except tools that may delete or overwrite data, which includes tools
without hints about their effects.

fields.name: refreshConnectorTools
fields.description:
Connects to a connector, lists its tools again, and stores them, so it also
checks that Sourcegraph can reach the server and authenticate. Connectors
with per-user authorization use the current user's authorization.

fields.name: disconnectConnector
fields.description:
Removes the current user's authorization for a connector with per-user
authorization.

fields.name: setConnectorUserToken
fields.description:
Stores the current user's API token for a connector with per-user tokens,
after checking that the server accepts it.

fields.name: setConnectorDisabled
fields.description:
Turns a connector off or on for one kind of the current user's agents.
Connectors are on by default.

types.name: OutOfBandMigration
types.description:
An out-of-band migration is a process that runs in the background of the instance that moves
data from one format into another format. Out-of-band migrations

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique identifier of this migration.

fields.name: team
fields.description: The team that owns this migration (e.g., code-intelligence).

fields.name: component
fields.description: The component this migration affects (e.g., codeintel-db.lsif_data_documents).

fields.name: description
fields.description: A human-readable summary of the migration.

fields.name: introduced
fields.description:
The Sourcegraph version in which this migration was introduced. The format of this version
includes only major and minor parts separated by a dot. The patch version can always be assumed
to be zero as we'll never introduce or deprecate an out-of-band migration within a patch release.

It is necessary to completely this migration in reverse (if destructive) before downgrading
to or past this version. Otherwise, the previous instance version will not be aware of the
new data format.

fields.name: deprecated
fields.description:
The Sourcegraph version by which this migration is assumed to have completed. The format of
this version mirrors introduced and includes only major and minor parts separated by a dot.

It is necessary to have completed this migration before upgrading to or past this version.
Otherwise, the next instance version will no longer be aware of the old data format.

fields.name: progress
fields.description: The progress of the migration (in the forward direction). In the range [0, 1].

fields.name: created
fields.description: The time the migration record was inserted.

fields.name: lastUpdated
fields.description: The last time the migration progress or error list was updated.

fields.name: nonDestructive
fields.description:
If false, the migration moves data destructively, and a previous version of Sourcegraph
will encounter errors when interfacing with the target data unless the migration is first
run in reverse prior to a downgrade.

fields.name: applyReverse
fields.description: If true, the migration will run in reverse.

fields.name: errors
fields.description:
A list of errors that have occurred while performing this migration (in either direction).
This list is bounded by a maximum size, and older errors will replaced by newer errors as
the list capacity is reached.

This type would more accurately be called "CodeGraphIndexJobState"
as it covers both precise and syntactic indexing.

See https://sourcegraph.com/docs/code-search/code-navigation/auto_indexing#lifecycle-of-an-indexing-job
and https://sourcegraph.com/docs/code-search/code-navigation/explanations/uploads#lifecycle-of-an-upload
for details about state transitions.

enumValues.name: WRITING
enumValues.description:
The index was processed and is being written into the new code intelligence store.
It becomes COMPLETED, and is used for code navigation, once it is written.

types.name: PreviewLicenseKeyResult
types.description:
Result of validating/previewing a license key.
If error is null, the license is valid and the other fields will be populated.
If error is non-null, the license is invalid and the other fields will be null.

fields.name: error
fields.description: If the license is invalid, this contains the error message.

fields.name: plan
fields.description:
The plan/product name associated with this license (e.g., "Sourcegraph Enterprise").
Only present if isValid is true.

fields.name: userCount
fields.description:
The maximum number of users allowed by this license.
A value of 0 means unlimited users (no seat cap will be enforced).
Only present if isValid is true.

fields.name: expiresAt
fields.description:
The expiration date of this license.
Only present if isValid is true.

fields.name: tags
fields.description:
Tags associated with this license (e.g., "trial", "dev").
Only present if isValid is true.

types.name: PreviewRepositoryComparison
types.description: A not-yet-committed preview of a diff on a repository.

fields.name: baseRepository
fields.description: The repository that is the base (left-hand side) of this comparison.

fields.name: fileDiffs
fields.description: The file diffs for each changed file.

args.name: first
args.description:
Return the first n file diffs from the list. If 0, no file diffs are returned, but totalCount and
diffStat describe the entire diff.

args.name: after
args.description: Return file diffs after the given cursor.

args.name: paths
args.description: A list of paths or directories used to filter the diffs

types.name: ProductSubscriptionStatus
types.description: Information about this site's product subscription (which enables access to and renewals of a product license).

fields.name: productNameWithBrand
fields.description: The full name of the product in use, such as "Sourcegraph Enterprise".

fields.name: offerUpgrade
fields.description:
Whether the UI should offer upgrading to a paid plan, for example because
this instance is on the free plan.

fields.name: actualUserCount
fields.description:
The max number of user accounts that have been active on this Sourcegraph site for the current license.
If no license is in use, returns zero.

fields.name: actualUserCountDate
fields.description:
The date and time when the max number of user accounts that have been active on this Sourcegraph site for
the current license was reached. If no license is in use, returns an empty string.

fields.name: maximumAllowedUserCount
fields.description:
The number of users allowed. If there is a license, this is equal to ProductLicenseInfo.userCount. Otherwise,
it is the user limit for instances without a license.

A value of 0 means unlimited users: no seat cap is enforced on this instance.

fields.name: allowsTrueUp
fields.description:
Whether the subscription allows true-up for user accounts. Those additional seats will be charged at the
next renewal.

fields.name: expiresAt
fields.description:
The date when this license expires. Null, if the license is valid indefinitely.
Enterprise subscriptions always expire, but other gating providers (workspaces)
may have a concept of non-expiry, when self-serve billing is enabled.

fields.name: isValid
fields.description:
This indicates if the current license is valid. It will be false if:
- The license key has expired
- The license key is in use on another instance
- The license key was revoked

fields.name: licenseInvalidityReason
fields.description: This indicates the reason the license is invalid. It'll be null if `isValid` is true.

Query the repository by a Git clone URL (format documented here: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone_git_urls_a_id_urls_a)
by checking for a code host configuration that matches the clone URL.
Will not actually check the code host to see if the repository actually exists.

args.name: name
args.description: Query the repository by name, for example "github.com/gorilla/mux".

args.name: cloneURL
args.description:
Query the repository by a Git clone URL (format documented here: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone_git_urls_a_id_urls_a)
by checking for a code host configuration that matches the clone URL.
Will not actually check the code host to see if the repository actually exists.

for example "github.com/sourcegraph/sourcegraph" -> "a6c905ceb7dec9a565945ceded8c7fa4154250df8b928fb40673b535d9a24c2f"

fields.name: usagesForSymbol
fields.description:
Identify usages for either a semantic symbol, or the symbol(s) implied
by a source range.
Ordering and uniqueness guarantees:
1. The usages returned will already be de-duplicated.
2. Results are first grouped by provenance in the order precise, syntactic, then search-based.
3. Results for a single repository are contiguous.
4. Results for a single file are contiguous.
Related: See `codeGraphData` on GitBlob.

EXPERIMENTAL: This API may make backwards-incompatible changes in the future.

In that case, `Usage.symbol.name` can be used to group results.
