fields.name: changeRequest
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Looks up a synchronized code-host change request by ID. Returns
null if it does not exist or the viewer can't access its repository (see
changeRequests). Only signed-in users can look up change requests, and only
while the bacon feature flag is enabled.

fields.name: codeHostCapabilities
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Code-host capabilities for a changeset and the viewer's linked
account. Requires the same access as changeRequest. Capabilities are scoped
to this changeset, not global properties of the code host.

fields.name: changeRequestReport
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Looks up a review report by ID. Any viewer who can look up
change requests and access the report's repository can open a report by ID,
not only its creator. Returns null if it does not exist or the repository
is not available to the viewer.

fields.name: changeRequestByRepository
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Looks up a synchronized code-host change request by repository
and number. Returns null if it does not exist or the viewer can't access its
repository (see changeRequests). Only signed-in users can look up change
requests, and only while the bacon feature flag is enabled.

args.name: repository
args.description:
Code-host-qualified repository name, such as github.com/owner/name.
Does not require the repository to be indexed by Sourcegraph.

args.name: number
args.description: The positive change request number on the code host, such as 123.

fields.name: reviewSemgrepConnection
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: The Semgrep connection that provides security scan results
for changesets, or null if Semgrep is not connected. Requires the
INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#READ permission and the bacon feature flag.

fields.name: compendia
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Compendia, AI-written long-form articles that walk the
reader through part of a codebase. Behind the compendia feature flag and
the COMPENDIA#READ permission; every field errors for a viewer without
them.

fields.name: connectors
fields.description:
The connectors (MCP servers) administrators configured for all users,
ordered by name. Every user can list them to see which ones they still need
to authorize. Users' personal connectors are listed by User.connectors.

args.name: first
args.description: Returns the first n connectors from the list.

args.name: after
args.description: Opaque pagination cursor.

fields.name: discoverConnector
fields.description:
Checks the MCP server at url before a connector is created: its name,
whether it requires authentication, and whether connectors can use OAuth
with it, like createConnector does.

Checks for personal connectors (personal: true) behave like personal
connectors: they require the CONNECTORS#WRITE_USER permission, and they can
only reach servers on public addresses, so they can't check servers on
private networks. Other checks require the INTEGRATION_MANAGEMENT#WRITE
permission.

fields.name: mcpConfig
fields.description: Configuration for MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration.

QueuedEvent represents a telemetry event that is queued for export. Events are
removed from this result set as they are exported.

fields.name: id

fields.name: queuedAt
fields.description: The time this event was queued for export.

fields.name: payload
fields.description: The raw event payload that is queued for export, rendered as JSON.

types.name: QueuedEventsConnection
types.description:
A list of telemetry events currently queued for export. Events are removed
from this result set as they are exported.

fields.name: nodes

fields.name: totalCount
fields.description: The total number of events in the connection.

fields.name: pageInfo
fields.description: Pagination information.

types.name: QuotaCheckResult
types.description: Result of a quota check.

fields.name: blocked
fields.description: True iff a request for this SKU would be rejected by CheckQuota right now.

types.name: QuotaSKU
types.description: Identifier for a quota-limited feature.

types.name: RandomizeUserPasswordResult
types.description: The result for Mutation.randomizeUserPassword.

fields.name: resetPasswordURL
fields.description:
The reset password URL that the user must visit to sign into their account again. If the builtin
username-password authentication provider is not enabled, this field's value is null.

If email sending (SMTP) is configured on this instance, an email containing this URL
will also be sent to the primary email address associated with the user.

fields.name: emailSent
fields.description:
If true, then an email with the password reset URL was sent to the primary email
address associated with the user. If false, email sending (SMTP) might not be configured
on this instance, or an error may have occurred - check the error logs with log scope
'randomizeUserPassword' for more details.

types.name: Range
types.description:
A range inside a file. The start position is inclusive, and the end position is exclusive.

Invariant: start <= end, where the start == end case is a zero-length range.

fields.name: start
fields.description: The start position of the range (inclusive).

fields.name: end
fields.description: The end position of the range (exclusive).

types.name: RangeInput
types.description:
A range inside a particular blob, describing a usage of a symbol,
which can be used to locate other usages of the same symbol.

The range must be an *exact match*.

In general, a single range may correspond to multiple symbols.
A caller can further drill down on a specific symbol using SymbolComparator.

EXPERIMENTAL: This type may make backwards-incompatible changes in the future.

inputFields.name: repository
inputFields.description: The repository containing the initial usage for a symbol.

inputFields.name: revision
inputFields.description:
The revision containing the initial usage for the symbol.

Defaults to HEAD of the default branch if not specified.

inputFields.name: path
inputFields.description: The path containing the initial usage for the symbol.

inputFields.name: start
inputFields.description: Start position of the range (inclusive)

inputFields.name: end
inputFields.description: End position of the range (exclusive)

fields.name: limit
fields.description: The number of tokens the rate limiter refills in the specified amount of time.

types.name: Repository
types.description: A repository is a Git source control repository that is mirrored from some origin code host.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The repository's unique ID.

fields.name: databaseID
fields.description:
The repository's database ID.
NOTE: this is intended for debugging purposes only, and clients should
generally just use GraphQL IDs.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
The repository's name, as a path with one or more components. It conventionally consists of
the repository's hostname and path (joined by "/"), minus any suffixes (such as ".git").
Examples:
- github.com/foo/bar
- my-code-host.example.com/myrepo
- myrepo

fields.name: uri
fields.description: DEPRECATED: Use name.
fields.deprecationReason: Use name.

fields.name: sourceType
fields.description: The source of this repository from where it was imported / converted.

fields.name: description
fields.description: The repository's description.

fields.name: iconURL
fields.description: Repository icon URL, when provided by the code host metadata.

fields.name: language
fields.description: The primary programming language in the repository.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: The date when this repository was created on Sourcegraph.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description:
DEPRECATED: This field is unused in known clients.
The date when this repository's metadata was last updated on Sourcegraph.

fields.name: commit
fields.description: Returns information about the given commit in the repository, or null if no commit exists with the given rev.

args.name: rev
args.description: The Git revision specifier (revspec) for the commit.

args.name: inputRevspec
args.description:
Optional input revspec used to construct non-canonical URLs and other "friendly" field values. Used by
clients that must ensure consistency of revision resolution within a session/request (so they use full
SHAs) but also preserve the user input rev (for user friendliness).

fields.name: changelist
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Returns infomration about the given changelist of the perforce depot, or null if
no changelist exists with the given cid or it is not a perforce depot.

fields.name: firstEverCommit
fields.description: The first commit inside the repo

fields.name: mirrorInfo
fields.description:
Information and status related to mirroring, if this repository is a mirror of another repository (e.g., on
some code host). In this case, the remote source repository is external to Sourcegraph and the mirror is
maintained by the Sourcegraph site (not the other way around).

fields.name: externalRepository
fields.description:
Information about this repository from the external service that it originates from (such as GitHub, GitLab,
Phabricator, etc.).

fields.name: isFork
fields.description: Whether the repository is a fork.

fields.name: isArchived
fields.description: Whether the repository has been archived.

fields.name: isPrivate
fields.description: Whether the repository is private.

fields.name: externalServices
fields.description: Lists all external services which yield this repository.

args.name: first
args.description: Returns the first n external services from the list.

fields.name: cloneInProgress
fields.description: Whether the repository is currently being cloned.
fields.deprecationReason: use Repository.mirrorInfo.cloneInProgress instead

fields.name: textSearchIndex
fields.description:
Information about the text search index for this repository, or null if text search indexing
is not enabled or supported for this repository.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The URL to this repository.

fields.name: externalURLs
fields.description: The URLs to this repository on external services associated with it.

fields.name: defaultBranch
fields.description:
The repository's default Git branch (HEAD symbolic ref). If the repository is currently being cloned or is
empty, this field will be null.

fields.name: gitRefs
fields.description: The repository's Git refs.

args.name: first
args.description: Returns the first n Git refs from the list.

args.name: query
args.description: Return Git refs whose names match the query.

args.name: type
args.description:
Return only Git refs of the given type.
Known issue: It is only supported to retrieve Git branch and tag refs, not
other Git refs.

args.name: pointsAtCommit
args.description: Return only Git refs that point directly at the given commit.

fields.name: branches
fields.description: The repository's Git branches.

args.name: first
args.description: Returns the first n Git branches from the list.

args.name: query
args.description: Return Git branches whose names match the query.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: The repository's Git tags.

args.name: first
args.description: Returns the first n Git tags from the list.

args.name: query
args.description: Return Git tags whose names match the query.

fields.name: comparison
fields.description: A Git comparison in this repository between a base and head commit.

args.name: base
args.description: The base of the diff ("old" or "left-hand side"), or "HEAD" if not specified.

args.name: head
args.description: The head of the diff ("new" or "right-hand side"), or "HEAD" if not specified.

args.name: fetchMissing
args.description: Attempt to fetch missing revisions from remote if they are not found

args.name: ignoreWhitespace
args.description:
Ignore whitespace when comparing lines in file diffs, like git diff -w. Lines that
differ only in whitespace become unchanged lines with their content from head, and
files with only whitespace changes are omitted from fileDiffs. changedFiles and
totalDiffCount are not affected.

fields.name: contributors
fields.description: The repository's contributors.

args.name: revisionRange
args.description: The Git revision range to compute contributors in.

args.name: afterDate
args.description: The date after which to count contributions.

args.name: path
args.description: Return contributors to files in this path.

args.name: first
args.description: Returns the first n contributors from the list.

fields.name: viewerCanAdminister
fields.description: Whether the viewer has admin privileges on this repository.

fields.name: label
fields.description: A markdown string that is rendered prominently.

fields.name: detail
fields.description: A markdown string of that is rendered less prominently.

fields.name: matches
fields.description: The result previews of the result.

fields.name: codeIntelligenceCommitGraph
fields.description:
Information and status related to the commit graph of this repository calculated
for use by code intelligence features.

fields.name: stars
fields.description: The star count the repository has in the code host.

fields.name: keyValuePairs
fields.description: A set of user-defined key-value pairs associated with the repo.
fields.deprecationReason: Use repo.metadata instead. This field is a deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

fields.name: metadata
fields.description: A set of user-defined key-value pairs metadata associated with the repo.

fields.name: topics
fields.description: A list of GitHub or GitLab topics associated with the repo.

fields.name: diskSizeBytes
fields.description: The size of repo when cloned on disk
fields.deprecationReason: Use mirrorInfo.byteSize instead. This field is a deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

fields.name: isRecordingEnabled
fields.description: Returns true if command executed on the repo are recorded.

fields.name: recordedCommands
fields.description: Returns a list of all recorded commands for given repository.

args.name: limit
args.description:
Maximum number of recorded commands returned.
If a query specifies a limit higher than 40, it will be capped at 40.
The default value is 40. This prevents returning an excessive number
of recorded commands for performance reasons.

args.name: offset
args.description:
Skips initial "offset" number of recorded commands.
(Default: 0)

fields.name: activityGraph
fields.description:
The activity graph for this repository, showing commit counts over time.
Returns null if activity data has not been computed yet.

fields.name: indexConfiguration
fields.description: Gets the indexing configuration associated with the repository.

fields.name: codeIntelSummary
fields.description: Provides a summary of the most recent upload and index status.

fields.name: previewGitObjectFilter
fields.description:
The set of git objects that match the given git object type and glob pattern.
This resolver is used by the UI to preview what names match a code intelligence
policy in a given repository.

args.name: type
args.description: The type of Git object described by the configuration policy.

args.name: pattern
args.description: A pattern matching the name of the matching Git object.

args.name: first
args.description: When specified, indicates that this request should return the first N items.

args.name: countObjectsYoungerThanHours
args.description:
When specified, the total number of matching Git objects younger than this value
will be returned along with the total number of matching objects. This does not
affect the set of objects returned as items.

fields.name: authorizedUsers
fields.description:
A list of authorized users to access this repository with the given permission.
This API currently only returns permissions from the Sourcegraph provider, i.e.
"permissions.userMapping" in site configuration.

args.name: permission
args.description: Permission that the user has on this repository.

args.name: first
args.description: Number of users to return after the given cursor.

args.name: after
args.description: Opaque pagination cursor.

fields.name: permissionsInfo
fields.description:
The permissions information of the repository for the authenticated user.
It is null when there is no permissions data stored for the repository.

fields.name: subRepositoryPermissions
fields.description:
Returns the sub-repository permissions for this repository.
Only site admins can use this query.

args.name: userID
args.description: The user ID whose permissions to view.

types.name: RepositoryComparison
types.description: The differences between two concrete Git commits in a repository.

fields.name: baseRepository
fields.description: The repository that is the base (left-hand side) of this comparison.

fields.name: headRepository
fields.description:
The repository that is the head (right-hand side) of this comparison. Cross-repository
comparisons are not yet supported, so this is always equal to
RepositoryComparison.baseRepository.

fields.name: range
fields.description: The range that this comparison represents.

fields.name: commits
fields.description: The commits in the comparison range, excluding the base and including the head.

args.name: first
args.description: Return the first n commits from the list.

args.name: path
args.description:
Filter to only the commits that modify files that match path.
Path can be either a file or a containing directory.

args.name: after
args.description:
Opaque cursor for forward pagination. Pass the endCursor returned in a
previous page's pageInfo to fetch the next page.

fields.name: fileDiffs
fields.description: The file diffs for each changed file.

args.name: first
args.description:
Return the first n file diffs from the list. If 0, no file diffs are returned, but totalCount and
diffStat describe the entire diff.

args.name: after
args.description: Return file diffs after the given cursor.

args.name: paths
args.description: A list of paths or directories used to filter the diffs

args.name: query
args.description: Filter files by path containing this search string

fields.name: totalDiffCount
fields.description:
The total number of files changed in this comparison.
This is more efficient than counting all file diffs when only the total count is needed.

fields.name: changedFiles
fields.description:
The list of files that changed in this comparison.
This is more efficient than fileDiffs when only file paths and statuses are needed.

args.name: first
args.description: Return the first n changed files. Defaults to 1000 and is capped at 5000.

args.name: after
args.description: Return changed files after the given cursor.

fields.name: anchoredThreads
fields.description:
EXPERIMENTAL: Threads anchored to this diff by the current user.
This field may change or be removed without warning.

fields.name: diffTour
fields.description:
An AI-generated guided tour that groups the changed files in this comparison
into thematic sections, each with a heading and summary.

Requesting this field kicks off generation if no tour exists yet and returns
immediately with status QUEUED (content fields null); it never blocks waiting
for generation. Poll the field until status is COMPLETED, at which point the
content fields are populated. Returns null only when the feature is not
enabled or the comparison has no base/head commit.

Because reading this field triggers generation, clients should request it
only when the user actually wants a tour (e.g. opens the tour panel), not on
every comparison view.

args.name: force
args.description:
Regenerate the tour even if one already exists. This is a one-shot
command, NOT a poll parameter: send it once (e.g. on an explicit
"regenerate" action), then poll with force omitted. Polling with
force: true would re-queue the job on every request and never reach
COMPLETED.

types.name: RepositoryComparisonInterface
types.description: Either a preview or an actual repository comparison.

types.name: RepositoryConnection

fields.name: totalCount

The total count of repositories in the connection. This total count may be larger

This requires admin permissions and will return null for all non-admin users.
In some cases, the total count can't be computed quickly; if so, it is null. Pass
precise: true to always compute total counts even if it takes a while.

fields.name: pageInfo

fields.name: queueJobID

The opaque identifier of the queued job this fetch job ran as, if it was
queued. Unlike id, it stays the same when a queued job finishes and moves
to the fetch history.

fields.name: repository
fields.description: The repository fetched by the job.

fields.name: state
fields.description: The current or final state of the job.

fields.name: reason

fields.name: operation

fields.name: queuedAt
fields.description: When the job entered the queue.

fields.name: startedAt
fields.description: When the job started.

fields.name: finishedAt
fields.description: When the job finished.

fields.name: durationMs
fields.description: The elapsed job duration in milliseconds.

fields.name: refsChanged
fields.description: Whether the fetch changed any refs.

fields.name: defaultBranchTip
fields.description: The default-branch tip after the fetch.

fields.name: failureMessage
fields.description: The final failure message.

fields.name: commitDiscoveryDurationMs
fields.description: The commit discovery duration in milliseconds.

fields.name: commitDiscoveryRejectionReason
fields.description: Why Sourcegraph did not calculate commit discovery duration.

types.name: RepositoryFetchJobConnection
types.description: A cursor-paginated list of repository fetch jobs.

fields.name: nodes
fields.description: The fetch jobs in this page.

fields.name: pageInfo
fields.description: Pagination information for this page.

types.name: RepositoryFetchJobDiscoveryRejectionReason
types.description: The reason Sourcegraph did not calculate commit discovery duration.

enumValues.name: FETCH_FAILED
enumValues.description: The fetch failed.

enumValues.name: NOT_BACKGROUND_FETCH
enumValues.description: The fetch was not a background fetch.

enumValues.name: CLONE_OR_RECLONE
enumValues.description: The operation was a clone or reclone.

types.name: SymbolUsageKind
types.description:
Categorizes a usage based on its relationship to the symbol of interest.

This enum may be expanded in the future.

EXPERIMENTAL: This type may change in a backwards-incompatible way in the future.

enumValues.name: DEFINITION
enumValues.description:
Denotes a usage as being a definition.

interface Animal:
    sound()

class Dog implements Animal:
    sound() override { ... }

func makeSounds(animal: Animal, dog: Dog):
    animal.sound()
    //     ^---^ (1)
    dog.sound()
    //  ^---^ (2)

Here, usagesForSymbol for (1) will return a Definition usage for Animal.sound().
Similarly, usagesForSymbol for (2) will return a Definition usage for Dog.sound().

In the general case, a symbol may have multiple definitions.
Here are some examples:

1. Python allows for multiple inheritance, so the same field can
   be declared in multiple parent classes. In such a situation,
   even Precise results may have multiple definitions.
2. A function may have different definitions based on the build
   configuration, such as for macOS vs Windows. A precise SCIP indexer
   may unify all such definitions into a single index as SCIP
   currently (as of June 20 2024) doesn't support tracking build
   configuration.
3. Syntactic or search-based results may not be able to find the
   exact definition, so they may return a superset of the full set
   of definitions.

enumValues.name: REFERENCE
enumValues.description:
Denotes a usage as being a reference. References are unified across
the inheritance hierarchy. For example, consider the following pseudocode:

interface Animal:
    sound()

class Dog implements Animal:
    sound() override { ... }

func makeSounds(animal: Animal, dog: Dog):
    animal.sound()
    //     ^---^ (1)
    dog.sound()
    //  ^---^ (2)

Here, usagesForSymbol for both (1) and (2) will return Reference usages
for both Animal.sound() and Dog.sound().
- For (1), it makes sense to also return reference usages for Dog.sound()
  because 'animal' may actually be a Dog.
- For (2), it makes sense to also return reference usages for Animal.sound()
  because 'dog' value may be up-cast to Animal at some point and the
  and 'sound()' might be called on it after that.

enumValues.name: IMPLEMENTATION
enumValues.description:
Denotes a usage as being an 'implementation', generally of a method, interface
or similar (the exact terminology varies across languages - traits, protocols etc.).

For example, consider the following pseudocode:

interface Animal:
//        ^----^ (1)
    sound()
//  ^---^ (2)

class Dog implements Animal:
    sound() override { ... }

Here, usagesForSymbol for (1) will return an Implementation usage for Dog.
Similarly, usagesForSymbol for (2) will return an Implementation usage for Dog.sound().

As of June 20 2024, Implementation usages are only supported by
Precise indexers. Syntactic and search-based usagesForSymbol will mark all
such usages as Reference.

enumValues.name: SUPER
enumValues.description:
Denotes a usage as being a 'super', generally of a method, type or similar.
The exact terminology varies across languages and the syntax under question -
for functions, it might be 'superclass method', 'interface method', 'trait method' etc.
and for types, it might be 'superclass', 'interface', 'trait' etc.

For example, consider the following pseudocode:

interface Animal:
    sound()

class Dog implements Animal:
    sound() override { ... }

func bark(dog: Dog):
    //         ^-^ (1)
    dog.sound()
    //  ^---^ (2)

Here, usagesForSymbol for (1) will return a Super usage for Animal.
Similarly, usagesForSymbol for (2) will return a Super usage for Animal.sound().

As of June 20 2024, Super usages are only supported by
Precise indexers. Syntactic and search-based usagesForSymbol will mark all
such usages as Reference.

UI note: Strictly speaking, depending on the exact symbol and language under
consideration, 'Super' usages would be better be grouped under a heading like:

- Method specification (for methods satisfying the signature of an interface
  method in Go or Java)
- Interface (for types implementing an interface in Go or Java)
- Trait method (for methods satisfying the signature of a trait method in Rust)
- Trait (for types implementing a trait in Rust)

and so on. Due to this large variation across languages, we've chosen
to group all such usages under 'Super' for now.

Historical note: This was previously called 'prototype' in the old API.
However, 'prototype' has a specific meaning in C++ different from our usage,
so we recommend avoiding the term 'prototype' in the UI.

The resulting array may be empty if no language could be determined,
or it may have multiple entries if the language is ambiguous.

If there are multiple entries, they will be sorted in descending

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior
in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or
skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information
to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description:
A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a
__DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

enumValues.name: QUERY
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a query operation.

enumValues.name: MUTATION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a mutation operation.

enumValues.name: SUBSCRIPTION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a subscription operation.

enumValues.name: FIELD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment definition.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_SPREAD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment spread.

enumValues.name: INLINE_FRAGMENT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an inline fragment.

enumValues.name: SCHEMA
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a schema definition.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a scalar definition.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an object type definition.

enumValues.name: FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field definition.

enumValues.name: ARGUMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an argument definition.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an interface definition.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a union definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM_VALUE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum value definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object type definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object field definition.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description:
One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a
placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in
a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Field
types.description:
Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has
a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description:
Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an
InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and
optionally a default value.

fields.name: defaultValue
fields.description: A GraphQL-formatted string representing the default value for this input value.

types.name: __Schema
types.description:
A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all
available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for
query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of
types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that
type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name and description, while
Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields
they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types
possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields` and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

Explains why this element was deprecated, usually also including a suggestion
for how to access supported similar data. Formatted in
[Markdown](https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/).

directives.name: skip

args.name: if
args.description: Skipped when true.
